# Android frame metadata

`device_hub::parse_semu` keeps its existing borrowed `(keyframe, payload)` API and accepts both supported metadata layouts. A version-1 header occupies 16 bytes. Version 2 adds an eight-byte server timestamp, so its H.264 access unit begins at byte 24. Feeding that timestamp to a video decoder corrupts the input; the reader now removes the complete header.

The source reference is the complete installed `expo-device-hub@0.19.1` module `vendor/serve-emu/dist/shared/frame-meta.js`, SHA-256 `99b8084e0981fcde03e0377f29813ee2643cf4c70fa83848cffeeb74ae22e16d`. The fixture generator imports and executes its real `writeFrameMetaHeader` and `parseFramePacket` exports. It does not reproduce their algorithms. The fixture also records the official npm package integrity.

The corpus contains 338 observations: 258 recognized native packets, 25 legacy empty version-1 headers and 55 unrecognized or truncated inputs. It covers version-2 producer output, version-1 compatibility, reserved flag bits, safe and unsafe JavaScript timestamp ranges, payload sizes, truncated headers and unknown versions. Every recognized native payload and keyframe flag must match byte for byte. Existing empty version-1 behavior is retained explicitly; the native browser instead treats an empty header as raw data. Raw or unsupported inputs remain outside this specialized metadata reader's contract and return `None`; this API does not expose the browser parser's raw fallback or latency fields.

The old reader failed the actual version-2 writer corpus: a one-byte access unit was returned with eight timestamp bytes prepended. The same corpus must pass after the fix, alongside the existing device-hub tests. Run generation and Rust tests only through `tools/android-sandbox`, with the pinned installation mounted read-only and a private target directory. The generator rejects host execution. These are byte-vector tests; they do not start an emulator, run a JVM harness, extract a root filesystem, create symlink fixtures or remove filesystem trees. Live emulator frame/input acceptance remains a separate consumer proof.
